In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of resistance to antineopla-stic drugs and, particularly, to doxorubicine.
the analysis of the influence of the oncogene Ha-ras on chemosensitivity of human tumor cells to antineop-lastic agents.
the study of the sensitivity of Ha-ras-transforme NIH3T3 clones to antineoplas-tic drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ha-ras transformation of NIH3T 3 cells does not affect the sensitivity pattern to the tested antineoplastic drug.
Ha-ras oncogenesis is not a major determinant of cellular chemosensitivity.
Ha-ras oncogenesis is not a relevant determinant of chemosensitivity in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the cell lines studied, the expression of the Ha-rass oncogene is not associated with an increased resistance to the antineoplastic compounds used in this study.
Ha-ras oncogenic activity has little influence on the cellular chemosensitivity of transformed cells.
Ha-ras-transformant cell lines are as sensitive as normal NIH3T3 to a variety of antineoplastic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ha-ras proto- oncogene, which is activated in 30% of all human malignancies, has no role in sensitivity of transformed cells to antineoplas- tic drugs.
the Ha-ras proto-oncogene, when overexpressed or activated by point mutations, does not seem to play a role in chemoresistance to antineoplas-tic agents in NIH3T3 mouse fibroblasts.
the sensitivity pattern of normal and Ha-ras transformed cells to a panel of antineoplastic drug is not altered by Ha-ras oncogenic activity.
